proposals.relationship: Gu recalls Liang Qichao’s essays among the readings that shaped his youthful sense of public and scholarly responsibility.
proposals.evidence_note: Gu’s own1926preface in Hummel’s1931translation17–18 names two admired Liang essays and places them among other poetry, family, school and political experiences;176 recalls the earlier statecraft ambition. Richter1994,358/n6 separately reports his early journal reading and notes a translation nuance about the wider world. A bounded formative reading, not Liang’s sole influence, later unchanged nationalism, personal teaching or derivation of all source criticism from Liang. Chinese original and Liang essays unread.

proposals.relationship: Richter compares Gu and Liang’s late dating of the Laozi against Hu Shi’s earlier chronology.
proposals.evidence_note: Named scholarly mediation: Richter1994,373/nn39–42 distinguishes Gu’s style-and-mentality argument, Liang’s late-Warring-States placement and the other distinct participants Qian Mu and Feng Youlan. Hu’s rejection of their evidence is reported and retains Richter’s judgment that he did not establish his own dating. This is an undirected comparison of particular arguments, not a claim that Gu copied Liang or that their complete positions were identical. Original debate texts and Hu’s1933reply (reprinted in1937GushibianVI,387–410) unread.

proposals.relationship: Gu limits historical materialism’s use for textual authentication while accepting its value for studying ancient systems and ideology, as Richter reports.
proposals.evidence_note: Richter1994,375–376 quotes Gu’s GushibianIIIpreface7–8 and IVpreface22–23. Gu insists on specialist source criticism as a basis for reconstruction and rejects applying historical materialism indiscriminately; he expressly accepts other approaches and its value in appropriate studies. Target is Marxist historiography, not a personal attack on Marx or every Marxist historian. Existing reverse1273reports Li Ji/Liang Yuantong through Dirlik and remains exact. Original Chinese prefaces unread; source-mediated claims retain Richter’s attribution.
